item.title: AWS Introduces GetScopedCredentials API to Safely Scope Down Temporary Security Credentials
item.description:
AWS Introduces GetScopedCredentials API to Safely Scope Down Temporary Security Credentials

AWS has launched GetScopedCredentials, a new AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) API that enables you to scope down the permissions of existing temporary security credentials. This feature is designed to help secure workloads, such as AI agents, by ensuring they only have the minimum permissions needed to perform their tasks rather than the full permissions of the calling session.

🔍 Overview

GetScopedCredentials provides a programmatic way to generate narrower security credentials from those you already possess. You can assign each agent, sub-agent, or process its own credentials that carry reduced permissions, a shorter session duration, or both, while keeping the original caller’s AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identity.

Because GetScopedCredentials works by narrowing the credentials you already have, it acts as a building block that you can integrate directly into:

  • Agent frameworks
  • Continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines
  • Services that issue credentials to other components
  • Custom applications

🧩 How it works

To call the API, you must have valid temporary security credentials and the necessary permissions to call GetScopedCredentials. You can make the call using the latest version of the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) or the AWS SDK for your programming language.

The technical specifications of the API include:

  • Input Credentials: You can call the API with the temporary credentials you already use, including those from aws login, an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance profile, or an AWS Lambda function.
  • Scope Down Policy: In each call, you pass a scope down policy (an inline policy representing the maximum permissions) of up to 2,048 characters.
  • Intersection of Permissions: The resulting permissions are the intersection of the session’s effective permissions and the scope down policy. This ensures that permissions can only be reduced, never expanded.
  • Session Duration: You can request a shorter session duration, which cannot exceed the remaining duration of the calling session.
  • Chaining Calls: You can call GetScopedCredentials again using the resulting scoped-down credentials to restrict permissions or reduce duration even further. This allows an orchestrating agent to give sub-agents narrower access than its own.

💡 Common Use Cases

GetScopedCredentials can be applied whenever a workload requires narrower access than the session that initiates it. Notable use cases include:

  • Limiting AI Agent Actions: AI agents decide on actions at runtime based on prompts or tool output. By using GetScopedCredentials, you can restrict their actions to only what is required—such as read access to a single Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket—or explicitly strip away risky actions like deleting resources. Run your agents in sandbox environments, such as AWS Strands Box, to ensure they only access these restricted credentials.
  • Scoping Down Based on Runtime Context: Some workloads run under a single IAM role but require different permissions based on authenticated requests. For example, a multi-tenant application with a single IAM role that serves files from different prefixes in one S3 bucket can use a trusted credential broker to call GetScopedCredentials. The broker obtains credentials restricted to only the specific tenant’s prefix and passes them to the worker.
  • Just-in-Time Access: Securing tasks based on runtime data learned only after the workload begins.

#AWS #Security #IAM #AIAgents #CloudSecurity

Source: Scope down permissions of existing sessions using AWS STS GetScopedCredentials | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AWS re:Invent 2026 to Showcase AWS Continuum and Security for AI Agents
item.description:
AWS re:Invent 2026 to Showcase AWS Continuum and Security for AI Agents

The AWS Security, Identity, and Governance team has announced the security session lineup for AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas, running from November 30 to December 4, 2026. The event will showcase new developments in AWS Continuum, a service designed to automate security workflows, alongside sessions on governance and authentication for autonomous AI agents.

🔍 Overview

AWS re:Invent 2026 features nearly 120 security sessions across breakouts, chalk talks, workshops, code talks, builders’ sessions, and lightning talks. Security sessions begin Monday morning and run through Friday, with Tuesday and Wednesday sessions distributed across the Wynn, MGM Grand, and Caesars Palace. On Thursday, December 3, the Wynn venue hosts a full day of advanced security sessions with 78 sessions from 8:00 AM to 5:30 PM, the majority of which are at the 300 level or above. This includes 12 workshops, 11 builders’ sessions, and 22 chalk talks.

⚙️ Key Sessions for AWS Continuum and Security

The event includes dedicated sessions detailing the capabilities of AWS Continuum and secure architectures for AI workloads:

The Thursday keynote runs from 8:30 to 10:00 AM at The Venetian and is also streamed online.

item.title: AWS WAF Introduces New Security Analytics Dashboard
item.description:
AWS WAF Introduces New Security Analytics Dashboard

AWS has introduced a new security analytics dashboard for AWS WAF, providing a single global page to investigate traffic across all protection packs (web ACLs), Regional resources, and Amazon CloudFront distributions. This update builds on the 2024 traffic overview dashboard by offering a consolidated view that helps users act on findings faster.

🔍 Overview

The new dashboard is designed to help users investigate and contain threats faster while reducing false positives that block real customers. Key aspects of the update include:

  • A single global page for investigating traffic across all protection packs (web ACLs).
  • Coverage of Regional resources and Amazon CloudFront distributions.
  • No need to build or maintain a custom log analytics pipeline.
  • Built on full-fidelity request data rather than samples.
  • Two primary use cases demonstrated: investigating a traffic spike and tuning rules to reduce false positives.

🧩 How It Works

To access the dashboard, users navigate to the AWS WAF console and select “Security analytics” in the navigation pane. The interface allows users to narrow the view to specific protection packs and set time ranges.

  • Global View: The dashboard displays request data across all protection packs in the account. Selecting “All protection packs” shows a comprehensive view.
  • Traffic Breakdown: The top of the page shows total requests split by action: Allow, Block, CAPTCHA, and Challenge.
  • Charts and Widgets: The “Requests chart” visualizes traffic changes over time, while widgets below display top values for specific dimensions. Users can split the Requests chart by dimensions such as Host, Rule triggered, Country, or JA4.
  • Host Grouping: Grouping or filtering by Host identifies which domains are under attack or experiencing spikes, even when a single protection pack protects multiple domains or a domain spans several protection packs.
  • Labels and Detections: AWS Managed Rules add labels (e.g., Bot Control categories, verification status, and signals like non_browser_user_agent). Users can also create custom labels. Because labels are recorded even when a rule is set to count-only, filtering by a label shows what a rule detected across all protection packs without changing how traffic is handled.
  • Filters and Actions: Filters apply to the entire dashboard, updating the action split, Requests chart, widgets, and request list. Users can select any value in a widget to focus on it, remove it, or block it.
  • Request Details: For individual requests, the dashboard displays HTTP fields such as host, path, headers, user agent, and JA4 fingerprint. It also shows which detections and labels matched and whether each action was enforced or only counted.

⚙️ Key Details

Previously, accessing this level of detail required working from a limited sample of requests or setting up and querying custom AWS WAF logs. The new dashboard makes this data available directly. Additionally, the current dashboard view is saved in the user’s browser.

💡 Why It Matters

This tool allows security teams to move from reactive log analysis to proactive investigation and containment. By providing full-fidelity data without the overhead of maintaining custom pipelines, organizations can more effectively tune their rules to minimize false positives and protect their infrastructure.

#AWS #WAF #WebSecurity #CloudSecurity #DataAnalytics

Source: Introducing the new AWS WAF security analytics dashboard | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Databricks Mitigates and Patches Java4Shell OpenJDK Vulnerability
item.description:
Databricks Mitigates and Patches Java4Shell OpenJDK Vulnerability

Databricks has addressed the industry-wide OpenJDK vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) before its public disclosure. The company is protecting its platform and customers through a two-phase response: immediate mitigation and subsequent patching.

🔍 Overview

Prior to Java4Shell’s public disclosure, Databricks was already addressing the vulnerability. The company is protecting customers in two phases: quick mitigation to disable use of the vulnerable code, and then patching to replace the vulnerable code.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Databricks has applied the mitigation to its platform, disabling use of vulnerable code for all supported versions of Databricks Runtime.
  • The mitigation is not expected to have a meaningful performance impact on customers.
  • To apply the mitigation as quickly as possible, Databricks took the rare step of proactively restarting affected clusters.
  • While the mitigation blocks the attack, in an abundance of caution, Databricks will provide patched versions of supported Databricks Runtimes.
  • Databricks has no evidence to indicate any unauthorized access to its products, services, or customers’ data.

🚀 Availability

Customer Type Patch Delivery Method
Serverless platform customers Patches will be applied automatically
Classic cluster customers Customers need to restart their clusters
Customers running custom images Databricks is reaching out to them

💡 Why It Matters

Databricks has stated it has no evidence to indicate any unauthorized access to Databricks products, services, or customers’ data. The proactive mitigation and planned patching demonstrate the company’s response to the vulnerability.

#Databricks #Java4Shell #OpenJDK #Security #Vulnerability #CloudSecurity

Source: Java4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) assessment

item.title: How AWS Security Incident Response triages threat findings from GuardDuty
item.description:
How AWS Security Incident Response triages threat findings from GuardDuty

AWS Security Incident Response continuously triages threat findings from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub CSPM, a process where most work never surfaces as a customer-facing case. The service ingests these findings through Amazon EventBridge rules automatically deployed during onboarding, ensuring that active threats are evaluated while posture and compliance issues remain in existing remediation processes.

🧩 How it works

The automated triage process evaluates each finding payload against several data sources to determine if an activity is benign or requires action.

  • Data sources: The service assesses the finding payload, related AWS activity from AWS CloudTrail and Amazon VPC Flow Logs, AWS threat intelligence, and user-provided environment context.
  • Benchmarking: Findings are mapped against a profile of known-good activity specific to the customer’s environment.
  • Third-party integration: Findings from tools like CrowdStrike, Trend Micro, or Lacework sent to Security Hub CSPM are also ingested, provided they carry complete payload information including resource ID, account ID, timestamp, and threat details. GuardDuty findings are ingested directly to prevent duplication.

⚙️ Key details

Outcomes of the triage process vary depending on the nature of the finding. Posture and compliance findings, such as misconfigurations or failed benchmark checks, are not triaged as they reflect environment state rather than active threats. They remain current without archiving and do not generate cases.

For active threat findings, such as compromised credentials, cryptomining, or data exfiltration, the service determines one of three dispositions:

Disposition Trigger Condition Action Taken
Archived, no action needed Automated triage or engineer confirms activity is benign or expected Finding is archived in GuardDuty; no case is created and no customer contact is made
Proactive case opened Triage cannot confirm activity is benign Case is opened as “Unconfirmed Activity” or “Inappropriate/Unintended Activity”; incident response team is engaged; finding stays Current until resolved
Retained for review Posture-related findings (e.g., overly permissive policies) No case is created; finding remains Current without archiving

When a proactive case is opened, customers respond via the AWS Management Console under the Cases section, allowing direct communication, context sharing, and case resolution. For third-party findings ingested through Security Hub CSPM, the disposition logic mirrors GuardDuty, but the status changes from NEW to NOTIFIED when triage begins, moving to SUPPRESSED if cleared as benign.

💡 Why it matters

The service builds a profile of what is normal in your environment to distinguish between expected behavior and genuine threats. For example, if GuardDuty flags an “UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS” finding, the service checks if the external IP belongs to a known corporate VPN range. If the pattern is recognized, the finding is archived. If the IP is from a hosting provider with no prior association and the IAM role has never called from outside AWS, a proactive case is created for investigation. Across customers, less than 1 percent of ingested findings result in a customer-facing escalation.

#AWS #Security #GuardDuty #IncidentResponse #ThreatDetection

Source: How AWS Security Incident Response triages your security findings | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Integrates with Okta Cross App Access for Secure Agent Governance
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Integrates with Okta Cross App Access for Secure Agent Governance

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale using any framework or model. A new integration with Okta Cross App Access (XAA) allows organizations to manage agent identity and governance directly within their identity provider (IdP).

🔍 Overview

This solution establishes a clear separation between governance and execution. Okta serves as the governance plane, deciding which agent may act for which user against specific resources. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore serves as the execution plane, managing credentials and turning governance decisions into valid access tokens.

Component Role
Okta Governance plane: decides which agent acts for which user against which resource.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity Execution plane: holds credentials and redeems grants for tokens in a vault.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime Validates Okta’s grant.

🧩 How it works

The identity flow ensures that agent actions are always tied to a verified user session:

  • User Sign-in: Users access a backend for frontend (BFF) using OpenID Connect via the agent’s linked Okta app.
  • Token Exchange: For each request, the BFF performs an RFC 8693 token exchange, trading the user’s ID token for an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) at Okta’s authorization server.
  • Okta Verification: Okta checks that the agent is active, the user is assigned to it, and an administrator has approved the applications and scopes the agent might reach.
  • Execution: The BFF invokes the agent on the AgentCore runtime using the ID-JAG. AgentCore Identity then redeems the ID-JAG for a short-lived access token accepted by the resource.

⚙️ Key details

The system utilizes three distinct tokens to record different decisions throughout the request lifecycle:

  • ID Token: Identifies the user.
  • Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG): Represents Okta’s decision; single-use and expires in 5 minutes.
  • Access Token: Issued by Okta’s custom authorization server, naming both the user and the agent.

In testing, the governance process proved highly responsive. When an administrator removed a user’s assignment, Okta refused new agent requests for that user within approximately 1 second. Existing tokens expired within 5 minutes. Performance testing showed that AgentCore Identity added roughly 0.6 seconds of latency to a request taking 30 seconds end to end.

🚀 Availability

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore charges based on usage. A technical walkthrough for building a task agent with this governance model takes about 1 hour. The associated sample code is provided for non-production use, and organizations should consult with security and legal teams before deployment.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #Okta #AIagents #Cybersecurity

Source: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 1 | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Orca Security Deploys Discovery AI on AWS Bedrock to Simplify Cloud Queries
item.description:
Orca Security Deploys Discovery AI on AWS Bedrock to Simplify Cloud Queries

Orca Security has released an update to its Discovery AI service, a natural‑language query agent built on Amazon Bedrock that translates plain‑English questions into Sonar queries for its cloud‑security data graph.

🔍 Overview

  • Security analysts need fast answers about their cloud infrastructure without deep familiarity with domain‑specific query languages.
  • Orca Security’s Sonar system tracks more than 900 cloud resource models (e.g., Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon S3 buckets) and requires JSON queries that specify exact model names, select from 18 operators, and navigate parent‑child hierarchies.
  • The original proof‑of‑concept loaded the full Sonar schema (over 900 model definitions) into a single prompt, yielding strong output but high token consumption (~2 million input tokens per workload), high latency (~60 seconds), and limited accuracy on complex multi‑model queries.
  • To address these issues, Orca partnered with AWS to build Discovery AI, a hybrid Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) solution on Amazon Bedrock that converts natural language into validated Discovery filters.

🧩 How It Works

Discovery AI follows a nine‑step pipeline, matching each stage to the most suitable Bedrock model:

  1. Request Entry and Context Setup – Combines the user’s question with organization, connected cloud providers, and request metadata.
  2. Quick Deterministic Matcher – Uses regex and rule‑based matching to detect high‑confidence patterns such as IP addresses, CVEs, ARNs, file hashes, AMI IDs, Oracle Cloud identifiers, EC2 IDs, URLs, and alert IDs.
  3. Fast‑Path Return – When a deterministic match is found, a predefined Discovery filter is returned without invoking an LLM.
  4. (Subsequent stages) – For unmatched requests, the pipeline proceeds through retrieval, schema‑aware construction, and LLM inference stages to produce a Sonar‑compatible JSON query.

Key design choices:

  • Amazon Bedrock provides access to multiple foundation models through a single API, allowing the team to allocate different models to each pipeline stage without separate integrations.
  • Bedrock inherits AWS governance controls (IAM, VPC endpoints, CloudTrail), satisfying Orca’s security requirements.
  • The model‑agnostic architecture enables swapping newer model versions without re‑architecting the pipeline.

⚙️ Key Results

  • Query costs reduced by 90 % compared with the baseline.
  • Input token usage reduced by 93 %.
  • End‑to‑end latency reduced by 75 %, achieving ~15‑second response times (down from ~60 seconds).
  • The system now handles thousands of queries per day.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Analysts can obtain answers without knowing Sonar’s exact schema or the 18‑operator query language.
  • Lower costs and faster responses make continuous cloud‑security monitoring more practical.
  • The hybrid RAG approach demonstrates how Retrieval‑Augmented Generation can be combined with domain‑specific schemas to improve accuracy on complex multi‑model queries.

#OrcaSecurity #AmazonBedrock #DiscoveryAI #CloudSecurity

Source: Natural language security queries at Orca Security using Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Bridgecrew launches Checkov for IaC and Open‑Source Package Security Scanning
item.description:
Bridgecrew launches Checkov for IaC and Open‑Source Package Security Scanning

Bridgecrew introduced Checkov, a static code analysis tool for infrastructure‑as‑code (IaC) that also performs software composition analysis (SCA) on container images and open‑source packages, helping developers prevent cloud misconfigurations and discover vulnerabilities early in the build process.

🔍 Overview

  • Checkov scans cloud infrastructure provisioned with Terraform, Terraform plan, CloudFormation, AWS SAM, Kubernetes, Helm charts, Kustomize, Dockerfile, Serverless, Bicep, OpenAPI, ARM Templates, or OpenTofu.
  • It also scans open‑source packages and images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs).
  • The tool powers Prisma Cloud Application Security, the developer‑first platform that codifies and streamlines cloud security throughout the development lifecycle.

🧩 How it works

  • Uses graph‑based scanning to provide context‑awareness policies.
  • Supports Python format for attribute policies and YAML format for both attribute and composite policies.
  • Detects AWS credentials in EC2 Userdata, Lambda environment variables, and Terraform providers.
  • Identifies secrets using regular expressions, keywords, and entropy‑based detection.

⚙️ Supported platforms

Category Supported Types
IaC templates Terraform, Terraform plan, Terraform JSON, CloudFormation, AWS SAM, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Dockerfile, Serverless framework, Ansible, Bicep, ARM, OpenTofu
CI pipelines Argo Workflows, Azure Pipelines, BitBucket Pipelines, Circle CI Pipelines, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI workflow files

📋 Key Features

  • Over 1 000 built‑in policies covering security and compliance best practices for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
  • Scans both IaC files and CI workflow definitions.
  • Performs Software Composition Analysis (SCA) for images and open‑source packages.
  • Provides context‑aware, graph‑based detection.
  • Enables policy authoring in Python and YAML.

🔐 Detection capabilities

  • Finds misconfigurations in IaC and cloud resources.
  • Detects AWS credentials in various locations.
  • Identifies secrets using regex, keywords, and entropy detection.
  • Scans container images and open‑source packages for CVEs.

🚀 Availability

  • Checkov is integrated into Prisma Cloud Application Security, delivering continuous security for cloud resources and IaC throughout the development lifecycle.

#Checkov #IaC #SCA #CloudSecurity

Source: bridgecrewio/checkov

item.title: Prowler Brings AI to Open Source Cloud Security Platform
item.description:
Prowler Brings AI to Open Source Cloud Security Platform

Prowler, the world’s most widely used open-source cloud security platform, now includes AI-driven capabilities to automate security and compliance across any cloud environment. This update positions Prowler as a platform that can “Secure ANY Cloud at AI Speed,” offering thousands of ready-to-use security checks and compliance frameworks.

🔍 Overview

Prowler is the Open Cloud Security Platform trusted by thousands to automate security and compliance in any cloud environment. With thousands of ready-to-use checks and compliance frameworks, Prowler delivers real-time, customizable monitoring and seamless integrations, making cloud security simple, scalable, and cost-effective for organizations of any size.

⚙️ Key Capabilities

Prowler now delivers AI-driven, customizable, and easy-to-use assessments, dashboards, reports, and integrations, making cloud security simple, scalable, and cost-effective for organizations of any size. Key features include:

  • Thousands of ready-to-use security checks, remediation guidance, and compliance frameworks
  • Prowler ThreatScore: Weighted risk prioritization scoring that helps you focus on the most critical security findings first

🏆 Supported Compliance Frameworks

Prowler includes hundreds of built-in controls to ensure compliance with a wide range of standards and frameworks:

Category Frameworks
Industry Standards CIS, NIST 800, NIST CSF, CISA, and MITRE ATT&CK
Regulatory Compliance and Governance RBI, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, and NIS2
Frameworks for Sensitive Data and Privacy GDPR, HIPAA, and FFIEC
Organizational Governance and Quality Control SOC2, GXP, and ISO 27001
Cloud-Specific Frameworks AWS Foundational Technical Review (FTR), AWS Well-Architected Framework, and BSI C5
National Security Standards ENS (Spanish National Security Scheme) and KISA ISMS-P (Korean)
Custom Security Frameworks Tailored to your needs

🚀 Availability

Prowler is available in two web application formats that simplify running Prowler across your cloud provider accounts:

  • Prowler Cloud: A hosted web application
  • Prowler Local Server: A self-hosted open-source version

Both provide a user-friendly interface to visualize the results and streamline your security assessments. For more details, refer to the Prowler Local Server documentation and try Prowler Cloud.

💡 Why It Matters

By integrating AI-driven assessments and threat prioritization into an open-source platform with thousands of built-in checks and extensive compliance framework support, Prowler makes cloud security more accessible and efficient for organizations of any size. The community is invited to join the Prowler community.

#OpenSource #CloudSecurity #AI #Compliance #DevSecOps #Prowler

Source: prowler-cloud/prowler

item.title: Wiz Hires Support Engineer with AI-Driven Automation Focus
item.description:
Wiz Hires Support Engineer with AI-Driven Automation Focus

Wiz, a cloud security company, published a job advertisement for a Remote Solutions Support Engineer based in Ireland, indicating a new role that combines deep technical troubleshooting with a growing emphasis on AI-driven automation to scale support operations.

🔍 Role Overview

The Remote Solutions Support Engineer will be part of a global team delivering expert-level technical support across the Wiz cloud-native security platform. The role involves investigating complex, multi-domain issues spanning cloud infrastructure, workload protection, vulnerability management, and runtime defense across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments.

  • 2+ years working with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) including IAM, networking, and core compute/storage services.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience deploying, managing, and troubleshooting production Kubernetes clusters and containerized applications.
  • Experience reading and debugging code in Python, Shell, JavaScript/JSON, Java, Go, or Terraform/HCL.

Wiz states it is redefining security for the AI era and is “powered by Google,” offering an AI-powered platform that harnesses Google’s Threat Intelligence and Security Operations. Visa sponsorship is not offered for this role. The position includes an after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-call rotation.

#Wiz #CloudSecurity #AIAutomation #Kubernetes #SupportEngineer

item.title: Benchling Secures AI-Generated Scientific Code Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Benchling Secures AI-Generated Scientific Code Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Benchling has implemented AgentCore Code Interpreter, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to securely execute AI-generated scientific code for researchers across thousands of tenants.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform designed to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale using any framework or model. Benchling utilizes this platform in Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) mode to handle several primary use cases:

  • AI agent-generated scientific code
  • Simple calculations
  • Code-generation sandboxes

🧩 How it works

To prevent data exfiltration and ensure tenant isolation, Benchling employs an architecture that separates production environments from code execution:

  • Production Account: Contains the Benchling Stack, IAM Roles, AWS STS, and customer data in Amazon S3.
  • Untrusted Code Account: A separate AWS account hosting the ACCI VPC and a container-based execution environment using gVisor for kernel-level isolation.

Tasks are dispatched from the production account to the untrusted account. Because the solution cannot use one IAM role per tenant to avoid unsustainable role sprawl, per-job credentials are injected into each session via AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to scope data access dynamically.

⚙️ Key details

Security is enforced through multiple layers of network and access controls:

Control Mechanism Function
VPC Configuration No internet gateway and no NAT gateway; restricts outbound paths to the public internet.
Security Group Restricts the Code Interpreter to port 443.
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall Applies a three-priority policy: blocks malicious domains (Priority 10), allows explicitly listed endpoints (Priority 100), and blocks all others (Priority 200).
VPC Endpoints Provides the only permitted network paths via S3 Gateway and Interface endpoints.
Network Controls Block HTTP, restrict egress ports, and limit outbound connections.

💡 Why it matters

This architecture ensures that each session accesses only that specific tenant’s data with no cross-tenant visibility. A Continuous Validation suite runs integration tests to simulate exfiltration attempts against the configuration. Currently, this architecture processes more than 600 code execution sessions per day across more than 250 tenants per week with zero security incidents.

#AmazonBedrock #AIagents #Cybersecurity #CloudComputing #AWS

Source: How Benchling secured multi-tenant AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Implementing Multi-Gate Authorization for MCP Tools on Amazon Quick
item.description:
Implementing Multi-Gate Authorization for MCP Tools on Amazon Quick

Amazon Quick now supports a multi-gate authorization pattern for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool invocations, utilizing an interceptor to evaluate OpenID Connect (OIDC) JSON Web Token (JWT) claims in sequence.

🔍 Overview

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that connects applications to internal tools, databases, and APIs to reduce the need for custom integrations. In this implementation, Amazon Quick connects to an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway—a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore—which provides the JWT validation layer and HTTP endpoint between clients and MCP tools.

🧩 How it works

Authorization is managed through a single AWS Lambda REQUEST interceptor attached to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. This interceptor processes JWT claims through four independent gates in a fixed sequence:

Gate Name Enforcement/Claim Purpose Requirement
1 MFA verification IdP / Conditional Access Policy Require MFA before token issuance Conditional
2 Country geo-fence ctry Restrict access to approved countries Conditional (REQUIRE_COUNTRY=true)
3 Group RBAC groups Map group membership to reader, author, or admin policies Always (core gate)
4 Tool permission Policy allowlists Verify the requested tool exists in the matched policy Always (core gate)

⚙️ Key details

  • Identity Provider: Microsoft Entra ID serves as the IdP. It enforces the Conditional Access Policy for MFA before issuing a token.
  • Configuration: Gates are configured via environment variables. While Gates 3 and 4 are always active, Gates 1 and 2 can be disabled by omitting the environment variables or setting them to false.
  • MFA Validation: Setting REQUIRE_MFA enables an additional check of the amr claim inside the interceptor for IdPs that record MFA evidence in the token.
  • Access Control: Role-based permissions establish a read/write boundary where readers can query risks but cannot create, update, or delete them, while administrators can bypass conditional gates.
  • Compliance: Every mutation must produce an immutable audit record for forensic and compliance requirements.

This pattern is demonstrated using a fictional example involving AnyCompany Global Services, which uses MCP tools on Amazon Quick to access a multi-tenant risk register hosted on Amazon DynamoDB.

Source: Implementing defense-in-depth authorization for MCP tools on Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick
item.description:
Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick

Quick has introduced architectural patterns to automate the assignment of custom permissions, allowing organizations to enforce fine-grained access control across the user lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

Custom permissions enable administrators to toggle specific features on or off for individual users. This allows for precise control, such as enabling financial analysts to author reports without exporting raw data, or allowing external partners to view dashboards without accessing sharing controls.

Permissions follow a three-level hierarchy where settings are applied as follows:

  • User-level: Overrides role-level settings.
  • Role-level: Overrides account-level settings.
  • Account-level: The base level of the hierarchy.

🧩 How it works

Organizations can use four architectural patterns to automate permissions based on their specific needs:

Method Application Scenario
RegisterUser API Applies permissions during user creation via the --custom-permissions-name parameter; common for SaaS companies restricting features like GenBI and paginated reports based on pricing tiers.
UpdateAccountCustomPermission API Sets a fallback profile for any user without an explicit assignment, including those created via Just-In-Time provisioning.
UpdateRoleCustomPermission API Sets a default custom permission profile per Quick role (READER, AUTHOR, ADMIN, and PRO roles).
Event-Driven Automation Uses Amazon EventBridge and AWS Lambda to detect new group memberships (native Quick groups or AWS IAM Identity Center groups) and apply permissions dynamically.

⚙️ Key details

  • Conditional Logic: For requirements beyond native defaults—such as applying different profiles based on group membership—event-driven automation is used. This is necessary because there is no native API for assigning custom permissions directly to a Group.
  • Complementary Strategies: Role and account-level defaults (Scenario 2) and group-based automation (Scenario 3) are complementary rather than alternatives.
  • Provisioning Gaps: Because Just-In-Time federation creates a window between account creation and group assignment, Scenario 3 only triggers upon the group membership event.
  • Enterprise Scale: Account-level defaults allow large enterprises to instantly block new features, such as GenBI or connectors, for all users during security reviews without per-user automation.

#Quick #AWS #AccessControl #Automation #IAM

Source: Automate user-level custom permissions for Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
